evidence.abstract: Under the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality targets, electro-hydrogen synergetic systems have emerged as a promising pathway for cross-temporal energy conversion and deep decarbonization across power, transport, and industrial sectors via the electricity-hydrogen-electricity. The system can enhance renewable energy integration, improve grid resilience, and support low-carbon transitions in hard-to-abate sectors. However, their large-scale deployment is still constrained by bottlenecks in key materials, efficiency coordination, dynamic matching, safety, and techno-economic performance. The review develops a framework spanning materials, components, systems, and market applications, with a focus on key material innovation, multi-timescale regulation, and full-chain integration. First, recent advances and critical challenges in water electrolysis technologies, including PEM, ALK, AEM, and SOEC, are reviewed in terms of catalyst materials, membrane electrode structures, stack-level in situ diagnostics, and durability under fluctuating operating conditions. Second, high-pressure gaseous, cryogenic liquid, and solid-state hydrogen storage pathways are comparatively assessed, revealing trade-offs among energy density, efficiency loss, safety, cost, and infrastructure compatibility. Third, the review summarizes coupling architectures for electricity-hydrogen-heat-gas multi-energy systems, as well as dynamic response control and multi-timescale optimal scheduling from microgrids and industrial parks to regional integrated energy systems. Finally, the application potential of electro-hydrogen synergetic systems in renewable energy consumption, grid ancillary services, and industrial decarbonization is discussed, and key scientific questions and suggestions for large-scale demonstration and commercialization are proposed.

evidence.title: Transmission and Conversion of Energy by Coupled Soft Gears
evidence.abstract: Dynamical aspects of coupled deformable gears are investigated to clarify the differences of mechanical properties between the machines consist of hard materials and those of soft materials. In particular, the performances of two functions, the transmission and the conversion of the energy, are compared between the hard and soft gears systems. First, the responses of the coupled gears against a constant torque working on one of gears are focused for two types of couplings; P) a pair gears are coupled, and T) three gears are coupled with forming a regular triangle. In systems with the coupling P), we obtain trivial results that the rotational energy can be transmitted to other gear only if these gears are hard enough. On the other hand, in systems with the coupling T), the transmission of the rotational energy to one of the other gears appears only if these gears are soft enough. Second, we show the responses of this system in which one of gears have contact with a high temperature heat bath and the other gears have contact with a 0 temperature heat bath. With the coupling T), the directional rotations appear in two gears having contact with 0 temperature heat bath. Here, the direction of these rotations change depending on the noise strength.

evidence.title: Effect of Lubricants on the Rotational Transmission between Solid-State Gears
evidence.abstract: Lubricants are widely used in macroscopic mechanical systems to reduce friction and wear. However, on the microscopic scale, it is not clear to what extent lubricants are beneficial. Therefore, in this study, we consider two diamond solid-state gears at the nanoscale immersed in different lubricant molecules and perform classical MD simulations to investigate the rotational transmission of motion. We find that lubricants can help to synchronize the rotational transmission between gears regardless of the molecular species and the center-of-mass distance. Moreover, the influence of the angular velocity of the driving gear is investigated and shown to be related to the bond formation process between gears.

evidence.abstract: This paper presents a modified grand canonical ensemble which provides a new simple and efficient scheme to study few-body fluid-like inhomogeneous systems under confinement. evidence.title: Modeling and Parameter Estimation of Automatic Transmission for Heavy-Duty Vehicle Using Dual Clutch Scheme
evidence.abstract: This paper focuses on modeling of the heavy-duty vehicle drivetrain with automatic transmission by using dual clutch scheme. The planetary gear set in the automatic transmission is complicated structure and difficult to understand. The advantage of the dual clutch scheme is that it can be used to represent the complex planetary gear set intuitively, which is a great help to understand the gear shifting process. It is also suitable for being used in the controller due to its low order. Some conditions are required to convert the planetary gear set to the dual clutch model. The heavy-duty vehicle driveline can be converted to the dual clutch model due to its heavy engine and vehicle inertia. This paper also proposes system prameter estimation methods to represent the driveline model. The main parameters are lumped inertia, lumped gear efficiency, output shaft compliance and friction coefficient of clutches. First, a method for estimating lumped inertia and lumped gear efficiency is proposed using WLSE(Weighted Least Sqaure Estimation) when gear is engaged. Second, resonance frequency of the system is obtained from the lock-up oscillation data occurring at the end of the gear shifting. The output shaft compliance is calculated by analyzing resonance frequency of the system. Third, the slip and friction coefficients of the clutch over time are calculated in the inertia phase. Using those data, the relationship between the dynamic friction coefficients and slip of the wet clutch can be obtained. Finally, a simulation is constructed to verify the accuracy of the proposed dual clutch model and the estimated system parameters. Simulation result is compared with experimental data.

evidence.title: High Fidelity Dog Clutch Model for Transmission Software Validation on a HiL System
evidence.abstract: Dog clutch is a type of mechanical clutch that are widely used in automotive transmissions for their ability to engage and disengage gear pairs rapidly between two rotating shafts or components without slippage, providing a direct mechanical connection. They offer positive no-slip engagement, higher efficiency, durability and can handle high torques. A real-time dog clutch model is necessary in software validation of transmission used in Electric Vehicles (EVs) on Hardware in Loop (HiL) Testing platform to ensures the data exchanged between electronic control unit (ECU) and the virtual environment occurs at the same rate as the actual system's operation, making the simulation as close to real-world performance as possible in a time-synchronized manner. However, modelling the behaviour of such dog clutch poses unique challenges due to their nonlinear dynamics, high-impact engagements, and as it needs precise control during shift operations. This paper describes a robust physics-based model of the dog clutch developed in MATLAB/Simulink suitable for testing the behaviour of transmission ECU on HiL testbench. Dog Clutch engagement process comprises of four primary states. Each state exhibit distinct dynamic behaviour. Dog clutch is modelled in two parts - first part is to simulate the model of dog clutch engagement and disengagement and second part explains modelling of dog clutch integrated with the automatic transmission system. Finally, the model was validated using data collected from the testbed measurements. Furthermore, the simulated results for engagement, disengagement and the transitions among the intermittent states of dog clutch were validated by comparing with actual measurement from testbeds. Such modelling methodology of dog clutch can be used on HiL which plays an important role in verification & validation (V & V) in development phase of EVs.

system.value: Transmission and Conversion of Energy by Coupled Soft Gears

abstract.value: Dynamical aspects of coupled deformable gears are investigated to clarify the differences of mechanical properties between the machines consist of hard materials and those of soft materials. In particular, the performances of two functions, the transmission and the conversion of the energy, are compared between the hard and soft gears systems. First, the responses of the coupled gears against a constant torque working on one of gears are focused for two types of couplings; P) a pair gears are coupled, and T) three gears are coupled with forming a regular triangle. In systems with the coupling P), we obtain trivial results that the rotational energy can be transmitted to other gear only if these gears are hard enough. On the other hand, in systems with the coupling T), the transmission of the rotational energy to one of the other gears appears only if these gears are soft enough. Second, we show the responses of this system in which one of gears have contact with a high temperature heat bath and the other gears have contact with a 0 temperature heat bath. With the coupling T), the directional rotations appear in two gears having contact with 0 temperature heat bath. Here, the direction of these rotations change depending on the noise strength.

system.value: Effect of Lubricants on the Rotational Transmission between Solid-State Gears

abstract.value: Lubricants are widely used in macroscopic mechanical systems to reduce friction and wear. However, on the microscopic scale, it is not clear to what extent lubricants are beneficial. Therefore, in this study, we consider two diamond solid-state gears at the nanoscale immersed in different lubricant molecules and perform classical MD simulations to investigate the rotational transmission of motion. We find that lubricants can help to synchronize the rotational transmission between gears regardless of the molecular species and the center-of-mass distance. Moreover, the influence of the angular velocity of the driving gear is investigated and shown to be related to the bond formation process between gears.

system.value: Modeling and Parameter Estimation of Automatic Transmission for Heavy-Duty Vehicle Using Dual Clutch Scheme

abstract.value: This paper focuses on modeling of the heavy-duty vehicle drivetrain with automatic transmission by using dual clutch scheme. The planetary gear set in the automatic transmission is complicated structure and difficult to understand. The advantage of the dual clutch scheme is that it can be used to represent the complex planetary gear set intuitively, which is a great help to understand the gear shifting process. It is also suitable for being used in the controller due to its low order. Some conditions are required to convert the planetary gear set to the dual clutch model. The heavy-duty vehicle driveline can be converted to the dual clutch model due to its heavy engine and vehicle inertia. This paper also proposes system prameter estimation methods to represent the driveline model. The main parameters are lumped inertia, lumped gear efficiency, output shaft compliance and friction coefficient of clutches. First, a method for estimating lumped inertia and lumped gear efficiency is proposed using WLSE(Weighted Least Sqaure Estimation) when gear is engaged. Second, resonance frequency of the system is obtained from the lock-up oscillation data occurring at the end of the gear shifting. The output shaft compliance is calculated by analyzing resonance frequency of the system. Third, the slip and friction coefficients of the clutch over time are calculated in the inertia phase. Using those data, the relationship between the dynamic friction coefficients and slip of the wet clutch can be obtained. Finally, a simulation is constructed to verify the accuracy of the proposed dual clutch model and the estimated system parameters. Simulation result is compared with experimental data.

system.value: High Fidelity Dog Clutch Model for Transmission Software Validation on a HiL System

abstract.value: Dog clutch is a type of mechanical clutch that are widely used in automotive transmissions for their ability to engage and disengage gear pairs rapidly between two rotating shafts or components without slippage, providing a direct mechanical connection. They offer positive no-slip engagement, higher efficiency, durability and can handle high torques. A real-time dog clutch model is necessary in software validation of transmission used in Electric Vehicles (EVs) on Hardware in Loop (HiL) Testing platform to ensures the data exchanged between electronic control unit (ECU) and the virtual environment occurs at the same rate as the actual system's operation, making the simulation as close to real-world performance as possible in a time-synchronized manner. However, modelling the behaviour of such dog clutch poses unique challenges due to their nonlinear dynamics, high-impact engagements, and as it needs precise control during shift operations. This paper describes a robust physics-based model of the dog clutch developed in MATLAB/Simulink suitable for testing the behaviour of transmission ECU on HiL testbench. Dog Clutch engagement process comprises of four primary states. Each state exhibit distinct dynamic behaviour. Dog clutch is modelled in two parts - first part is to simulate the model of dog clutch engagement and disengagement and second part explains modelling of dog clutch integrated with the automatic transmission system. Finally, the model was validated using data collected from the testbed measurements. Furthermore, the simulated results for engagement, disengagement and the transitions among the intermittent states of dog clutch were validated by comparing with actual measurement from testbeds. Such modelling methodology of dog clutch can be used on HiL which plays an important role in verification & validation (V & V) in development phase of EVs.

abstract.value: The main objective of this project is to provide a demand-based automatic shifting system for automobiles. The DASS automatically shifts gears and engages/disengages the clutch of a manual transmission automobile based on demand. This is accomplished with the use of an electro-mechanical system controlled by a microcontroller. The shifting algorithm is determined by throttle position (varying driver\u27s demand for acceleration), road speed, and engine state (engine\u27s revolution per minute). unlike other transmission system DASS combines the rigidity of a clutch system in a manual transmission for better energy transmission and the convenience of automatic shifting

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

However, on the microscopic scale, it is not clear to what extent lubricants are beneficial. The planetary gear set in the automatic transmission is complicated structure and difficult to understand. The advantage of the dual clutch scheme is that it can be used to represent the complex planetary gear set intuitively, which is a great help to understand the gear shifting process. The heavy-duty vehicle driveline can be converted to the dual clutch model due to its heavy engine and vehicle inertia. First, a method for estimating lumped inertia and lumped gear efficiency is proposed using WLSE(Weighted Least Sqaure Estimation) when gear is engaged. Second, resonance frequency of the system is obtained from the lock-up oscillation data occurring at the end of the gear shifting. The output shaft compliance is calculated by analyzing resonance frequency of the system. Third, the slip and friction coefficients of the clutch over time are calculated in the inertia phase. Using those data, the relationship between the dynamic friction coefficients and slip of the wet clutch can be obtained. custody_records.raw_content: Dog clutch is a type of mechanical clutch that are widely used in automotive transmissions for their ability to engage and disengage gear pairs rapidly between two rotating shafts or components without slippage, providing a direct mechanical connection. They offer positive no-slip engagement, higher efficiency, durability and can handle high torques. A real-time dog clutch model is necessary in software validation of transmission used in Electric Vehicles (EVs) on Hardware in Loop (HiL) Testing platform to ensures the data exchanged between electronic control unit (ECU) and the virtual environment occurs at the same rate as the actual system's operation, making the simulation as close to real-world performance as possible in a time-synchronized manner. However, modelling the behaviour of such dog clutch poses unique challenges due to their nonlinear dynamics, high-impact engagements, and as it needs precise control during shift operations. This paper describes a robust physics-based model of the dog clutch developed in MATLAB/Simulink suitable for testing the behaviour of transmission ECU on HiL testbench. Dog Clutch engagement process comprises of four primary states. Each state exhibit distinct dynamic behaviour. Dog clutch is modelled in two parts - first part is to simulate the model of dog clutch engagement and disengagement and second part explains modelling of dog clutch integrated with the automatic transmission system. Finally, the model was validated using data collected from the testbed measurements. Furthermore, the simulated results for engagement, disengagement and the transitions among the intermittent states of dog clutch were validated by comparing with actual measurement from testbeds.
